extra_misconceptions.fact: Intact blister skin forms a sterile barrier against bacteria, so leave small blisters unpopped and cushion them with a moleskin doughnut.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Popping every trail blister immediately with a pocketknife blade lets the skin heal faster while you keep walking.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Incising or sucking a snakebite damages tissue and introduces mouth bacteria; keep the limb immobilized below heart level and evacuate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting across a venomous snakebite and sucking out the venom stops the toxin from reaching the hiker's bloodstream.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Smothering or burning a tick causes it to regurgitate infectious fluids into the wound; pull it straight out with fine-tipped tweezers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Suffocating an embedded tick with petroleum jelly or a hot match makes it back out cleanly without leaving mouthparts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wet clothing and brisk wind in fifty-degree weather strip body heat fast enough to trigger hypothermia in an exhausted, underfed hiker.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hypothermia only happens when daytime or nighttime air temperatures drop below the freezing point of thirty-two degrees.

extra_socratic_questions: What immediate step prevents a friction hot spot on your heel from turning into a fluid-filled blister on the trail?
Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a steep summer climb?
What specific change in a hiker's speech or gait signals that mild cold exposure has progressed into hypothermia?
Why is it dangerous to rub frostbitten toes or warm them directly next to a campfire before hike evacuation is ready?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cotton holds moisture against the skin, softens the epidermis, and causes blisters; merino wool or synthetic socks wick moisture away.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Thick hundred-percent cotton athletic socks are ideal for long hikes because cotton absorbs large amounts of foot sweat.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Stepping off the tread to avoid mud tramples fragile trailside plants and widens erosion ruts; walk straight through the center of mud.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Skirting around the edges of trail mud puddles follows Leave No Trace by keeping your boots clean and off wet soil.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Stiff, unbroken boots create severe pressure points, so you must break them in gradually on short walks before attempting a ten-mile hike.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Brand-new leather hiking boots are ready for a ten-mile trek right out of the box if you wear two pairs of thick socks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hikers above horses can spook them into bolting off the ledge; step to the downhill side, speak calmly, and let stock pass on the inside.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stepping to the uphill side of a narrow trail gives pack animals and horses the safest room to pass below your group.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout group position itself and move when encountering pack horses on a narrow, sloped mountain trail?
Why does walking single file right through the middle of a muddy trail section protect the surrounding ecosystem?
What clearance test inside a laced hiking boot confirms your toes will not jam into the front cap on steep descents?
Under what road condition must hikers walk single file on the left shoulder facing traffic while wearing reflective gear?

extra_misconceptions.fact: All-out sprinting shifts muscles into anaerobic metabolism and builds lactic acid rapidly, whereas steady aerobic pacing sustains hours.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sprinting up steep hills until you are gasping for air builds hiking endurance faster than keeping a steady, rhythmic pace.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flat treadmills miss eccentric downhill braking and uneven ankle stabilization, so training must include hills, stairs, and trail terrain.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Conditioning only on flat gymnasium treadmills prepares all the leg muscles and tendons needed for rugged mountain trails.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Jumping mileage by more than ten to fifteen percent per week overloads tendons and bones, raising the risk of shin splints and stress injury.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Doubling your longest training hike distance from five miles straight to fifteen miles in one week safely speeds fitness.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Muscles and connective tissues repair and grow stronger during recovery periods, so a sound conditioning plan schedules regular rest days.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hiking every single day without rest days is the fastest way to strengthen leg muscles before a twenty-mile qualifier.

extra_socratic_questions: What weekly progression in mileage and pack weight safely prepares your joints and lungs for a full ten-mile trek?
What happens to muscle fatigue and breathing when your uphill pace pushes you past your aerobic threshold into debt?
What field check using your speaking voice confirms you are hiking within a sustainable aerobic heart-rate zone?
Why is it dangerous to train with your target twenty-mile pack weight during the very first week of conditioning?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 4 mandates twenty continuous miles completed on a single day, so split miles across two days cannot fulfill the twenty-miler.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Walking ten miles on Saturday morning and ten miles on Sunday afternoon on a weekend campout counts as the twenty-mile hike.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Closely spaced contour lines indicate steep elevation gain, which adds roughly one extra hour of hiking time per thousand feet of ascent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ten miles on a topographic map always takes the exact same number of hours regardless of how close the contour lines sit.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Simple sugars cause a sharp blood-glucose spike and crash; endurance hikers need complex carbohydrates, proteins, and fats for steady fuel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Candy bars and sugary soda alone make a complete trail lunch for a twenty-mile hike because sugar gives instant energy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Phone batteries die quickly in cold weather or weak signal zones, so every hiker must carry a paper map, compass, and working flashlight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A smartphone GPS app replaces a paper topographic map, magnetic compass, and headlamp on a clear daytime ten-mile hike.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must your written hike plan receive counselor approval and stay with a trusted contact before anyone steps on trail?
What adjustment to your estimated hiking time is required when a ten-mile map route includes two thousand feet of climb?
What map measurement besides horizontal trail distance determines whether a twenty-mile route can finish before sunset?
Which combination of trail lunch macronutrients provides both quick energy for climbs and lasting fuel for twenty miles?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Waiting weeks blurs route landmarks, weather shifts, and pacing lessons; write each report during the trek or right after finishing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saving all five hike reports to write from memory at the end of the season captures the same details as writing right away.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A GPS track lacks weather context, wildlife observations, personal takeaways, and explanations of how you overcame trail challenges.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pasting a screenshot of a fitness watch mileage summary fulfills the entire post-hike reflection report for your counselor.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Honest documentation of trail problems and the adjustments that solved them is the core purpose of requirement 5 and improves future hikes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hiding equipment mistakes, hot spots, or navigation errors in your hike report makes you look like a more capable Scout.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Written hike logs build a personal reference of pace rates, water consumption, and layer performance that prevents mistakes on longer treks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Post-hike reports are just paperwork for the badge counselor and have no practical value once the hike is finished.

extra_socratic_questions: Why does jotting field observations at rest stops produce a more accurate post-hike report than waiting until next week?
What specific detail turns a simple complaint about sore feet into a useful reflection on how you solved the challenge?
What weather and hydration numbers from your first ten-mile report help you pack better for your twenty-mile finale?
Which gear or clothing failures noted in an early hike report should trigger changes to your next written hike plan?
